1.note: Zechariah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [to a man he gives vegetation in the field]

Zechariah is not referring to a specific **man**. He means people in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [to each person]

2.note: The word **For** introduces the reason Zechariah gives for the command to ask Yahweh for rain rather than trusting in idols and diviners. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason.

Since **household idols** cannot speak, this represents the false messengers that claim to speak for the household idols. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the false prophets who profess to speak for your silent household idols speak iniquity]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **iniquity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [speak wicked things]

Zechariah is using the possessive form to describe **dreams** that are characterized by **the emptiness**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and they claim to have visions from their gods but they are just making things up]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **vanity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [worthlessly]

The point of this comparison is that just as **a flock** with no shepherd wanders and suffers, so do the people who rely on idols and diviners. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [they wander and suffer just as a flock wanders and suffers when there is no shepherd to guide them]

The pronoun **they** refers to the people, not to the idols or the diviners just mentioned. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the people journey like a flock]

Here Zechariah is speaking as if a leader who guides and protects people were a **shepherd**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [there is no leader to guide and protect them]

3.note: Here Yahweh begins to speak, but there is no verb introducing his words as a quotation. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this as a direct quotation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh says, “Against the shepherds my nose burns]

These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [I am furious with the shepherds who lead my people, and I will certainly deal with those leaders]

Yahweh is speaking of the leaders of the people as if they were **the shepherds** of a flock. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Some interpreters think these refer to the foreign leaders (see 11:3). Alternate translation: [the leaders who should be like shepherds]
Here, **nose ** represents Yahweh’s anger. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [I am furious]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the corrupt leaders of Judah as if they were **the male goats** who lead a flock. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the head goats of the flock] or [the leaders]

Here Yahweh is speaking of his anger as if it were a fire when he says that it burns. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my anger is intense]

The word **For** introduces the reason for what Yahweh has just said about punishing the leaders: he cares for his people and will restore them. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason.

Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as **Yahweh of Armies**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [For I, Yahweh of Armies, attend to my flock, the house of Judah, and I will make them]

Here Yahweh is speaking of his people as if they were **his flock** of sheep. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [his people]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the people of the kingdom of Judah as if they were a single house, or household. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the people of the kingdom of Judah]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **splendor**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [like his splendid horse]

The point of this comparison is that just as **the horse of his splendor** is strong and majestic **in the battle**, so the people of Judah will be. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [as strong and majestic in the battle as his splendid warhorse]

4.note: The pronoun **him** refers to Judah, mentioned in the previous verse. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [From him, that is, Judah, a cornerstone]
If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to move **will come forth** from the end of the verse to here at the start. Alternate translation: [From him will come forth a cornerstone]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the rulers who will come from Judah as if they were **a cornerstone** of a building, the **tent peg**, and **a bow of war**. Your language may have comparable expressions that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [will come forth the ruler who supports them … the ruler who holds them together … the ruler who leads them in war]

5.note: The pronoun **they** refers to the people of Judah. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the people of Judah will be like warriors]

The point of this comparison is that just as **warriors** are strong and victorious in battle, so will the people of Judah be. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [strong and victorious like warriors]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. The meaning may be that the warriors will trample their enemies into the mud of the streets. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [trampling their enemies in the mud of the streets in the battle]
The word **for** introduces the reason the people of Judah will prevail in battle: Yahweh is with them. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason.

By **Yahweh is with them**, Zechariah means that Yahweh will help them win the battle against their enemies. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will help them]

Here, the expression **put to shame** represents defeating them in battle. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and they will defeat the riders of horses]

6.note: The word **for** introduces the reason Yahweh will restore his people: he has compassion on them. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason.
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **compassion**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [I feel compassionate toward them]

Here, **house** means all the people descended from a particular person. It envisions them as if they were one household living together. So **the house of Judah** and **the house of Joseph** figuratively mean all the people descended from Judah and from Joseph. Alternate translation: [the people of Judah … the people of Joseph]

7.note: The word their is plural, but it refers back to Ephraim, which is grammatically singular. Here the singular name Ephraim stands for all the people of that tribe. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the people of Ephraim will be like a warrior, and their heart will be glad]

The point of this comparison is that just as **a warrior** is strong and courageous, so the people of Ephraim will be. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [And Ephraim will be as strong and courageous as a warrior]
Here the **heart** represents where a person’s feelings exist. You may have a comparable expression in your language, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [their feelings]

The point of this comparison is that just as **wine** makes a person feel glad and cheerful, so their hearts will be glad. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [as people become cheerful from drinking wine]

The point of this comparison is that just as a person who drinks **wine** becomes cheerful, so the people of Ephraim will be glad. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [their heart will be glad, just as a person who drinks wine becomes cheerful]

The point of this comparison is that just as **a warrior** is strong and mighty, so **Ephraim** will be. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [like a strong and mighty warrior]

In this verse, the word **heart** is singular in form, but it refers to all the people of Ephraim as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “heart.” Alternate translation: [and their hearts will be glad]

Here Zechariah is speaking as if a person’s **heart** were where their feelings exist. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [their feelings will exult]

8.note: Here the word **For** introduces not a reason but an explanation. You may want to use a different connecting word to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [after all]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if he were a shepherd who could **whistle** for his flock to gather them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will summon them]

9.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of scattering his people among the nations as if he were planting seed when he says that he will **sow them**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I will cause them to live among different nations]

10.note: Yahweh is referring to all the places from which he will bring his people back by naming two extremes, **the land of Egypt** and **Assyria**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [I will bring them back from every land, including Egypt and Assyria]

The expression **will not be found** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and they will not have enough room]

11.q: וְ⁠עָבַ֨ר בַּ⁠יָּ֜ם צָרָ֗ה וְ⁠הִכָּ֤ה בַ⁠יָּם֙ גַּלִּ֔ים וְ⁠הֹבִ֕ישׁוּ כֹּ֖ל מְצוּל֣וֹת יְאֹ֑ר
11.note: By **he will pass through the sea of distress, and he will strike the waves in the sea, and all the depths of the Nile will dry up**, Zechariah means that Yahweh will remove every danger and obstacle blocking his people’s return to their land, just as he dried up the sea and the Jordan for their ancestors when he brought them out of Egypt and into the land. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will clear away every danger that threatens his people, just as he dried up the sea and the Jordan for their ancestors]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the troubles his people face as if they were a dangerous sea when he refers to **the sea** of **distress**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the distress that is like a dangerous sea]

The pronoun **he** could refer to: (1) Yahweh. In the surrounding verses, Yahweh speaks of himself in the first person, but here he is referred to in the third person. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh will pass through the sea] or (2) Ephraim, that is the people of the northern tribes of Israel. However, in the surrounding verse Ephraim is always referred to using plural pronouns and verbs. Alternate translation: [And Ephraim will pass through the sea]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **distress**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the distressing sea]

Here Yahweh is using the phrase **strike the waves in the sea** as a common expression to mean that he will subdue the raging waters and overcome the troubles they represent. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he will subdue the raging waves in the sea]

The expression **will be brought down** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is Yahweh. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh will bring down the pride of Assyria]

Here, the term **pride** represents the proud nation of Assyria and its army. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And the proud army of Assyria will be brought down]

Here, the term **scepter** represents the royal power of Egypt, since a scepter is a symbol that a king holds. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and the royal power of Egypt will be no more]

12.note: Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as **Yahweh**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [And I will strengthen them in myself, and in my name they will walk]

Here Yahweh is speaking of how the people will live as if they would **walk** along a path. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they will conduct their lives]
Here, **his name** represents Yahweh’s authority. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and by his authority]

Zechariah is using the phrase **the declaration of Yahweh** to indicate that what has been said is a direct quotation from Yahweh and comes with Yahweh’s authority. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language.
